purpose: Increase high-level human evidence coverage using real systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and one umbrella review.
source_policy: Each record was checked against PubMed before inclusion. Evidence text is a curator-written summary of the PubMed abstract and is not represented as a verbatim quote.
overlap_policy: All PMIDs are unique and disjoint from the 64 human-evidence PMIDs already present in the uploaded project.

records.title: Effectiveness of Boswellia and Boswellia extract for osteoarthritis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.evidence_text: The meta-analysis found that Boswellia and its extracts reduced pain and stiffness and improved joint function compared with control treatment.

records.title: Effectiveness of Curcuma longa extract versus placebo for the treatment of knee osteoarthritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
records.evidence_text: Curcuma longa extract showed significant improvements in knee osteoarthritis pain and physical function compared with placebo.

records.title: The impact of peppermint oil on the irritable bowel syndrome: a meta-analysis of the pooled clinical data
records.evidence_text: Pooled clinical data favored peppermint oil over placebo for global irritable bowel syndrome symptoms and abdominal pain.

records.title: Cranberry Reduces the Risk of Urinary Tract Infection Recurrence in Otherwise Healthy Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
records.evidence_text: The systematic review and meta-analysis found that cranberry reduced the risk of recurrent urinary tract infection in otherwise healthy women.

records.title: Consumption of cranberry as adjuvant therapy for urinary tract infections in susceptible populations: A systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis
records.indication: urinary tract infection prevention in susceptible populations
records.evidence_text: Cranberry consumption was associated with a lower risk of urinary tract infection in susceptible populations in the pooled analysis.

records.title: Effect of green tea supplementation on blood pressure: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
records.evidence_text: Green tea supplementation significantly reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure in the pooled randomized trial analysis.

records.title: St. John's Wort for Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review
records.evidence_text: The systematic review found St John's wort more effective than placebo for major depressive disorder and broadly comparable with antidepressant medication for clinical response.

records.title: Effects of Garlic on Glucose Parameters and Lipid Profile: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on Randomized Controlled Trials
records.evidence_text: Garlic supplementation significantly improved several glucose and lipid parameters across randomized controlled trials.

records.title: Ginkgo biloba for prevention of dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.evidence_text: The meta-analysis found no convincing evidence that Ginkgo biloba prevents the development of dementia and did not support its use for this indication.

records.title: Black cohosh for the management of menopausal symptoms: a systematic review of clinical trials
records.evidence_text: The systematic review concluded that convincing evidence for black cohosh efficacy in menopausal symptoms remained to be demonstrated.

records.title: The preventive and relieving effects of ginger on postoperative nausea and vomiting: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
records.evidence_text: Ginger reduced postoperative nausea at several time points, but did not significantly reduce postoperative vomiting, combined nausea and vomiting, or antiemetic drug use.

records.title: Black cohosh extracts in women with menopausal symptoms: an updated pairwise meta-analysis
records.evidence_text: Black cohosh significantly improved overall menopausal symptoms and hot flashes, but did not significantly improve anxiety or depressive symptoms.

records.title: Effects of Ginkgo biloba in dementia: systematic review and meta-analysis
records.evidence_text: Ginkgo favored placebo for cognition in the meta-analysis, while activities of daily living did not differ significantly from placebo.

records.title: Therapeutic efficacy and safety of chamomile for state anxiety, generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, and sleep quality: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials and quasi-randomized trials
records.evidence_text: Chamomile showed benefit for generalized anxiety disorder and some sleep outcomes, while evidence across state anxiety, insomnia and sleep quality was not uniformly significant.

records.title: Ginseng as a Treatment for Fatigue: A Systematic Review
records.evidence_text: Some trials reported significant fatigue improvement with ginseng, whereas others did not, leaving the overall evidence inconsistent.

records.title: Rhodiola rosea for physical and mental fatigue: a systematic review
records.evidence_text: The systematic review found contradictory evidence for Rhodiola rosea in fatigue, with some trials reporting benefit and others not showing clear efficacy.

records.title: Does valerian work for insomnia? An umbrella review of the evidence
records.evidence_text: The umbrella review found heterogeneous and inconsistent evidence for valerian in insomnia, with signals of benefit but insufficiently consistent evidence for a definitive conclusion.

records.title: Efficacy of Ginger (Zingiber officinale) in Ameliorating Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting and Chemotherapy-Related Outcomes: A Systematic Review Update and Meta-Analysis
records.evidence_text: The pooled evidence showed benefit for some chemotherapy-related nausea outcomes, but effects were not consistent across nausea, vomiting and related endpoints.
